subject: Frontloaded multi-year prepay proposal & early-exit amendment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rinaldi <trinaldi@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Frontloaded multi-year prepay proposal & early-exit amendment

Tom —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, attached is a simple frontloaded prepay proposal that preserves Acme’s target economics through year 2 while giving a larger discount on year 1 (to help your 2026 budget). High level:

- 3-year term, $3.6M total commit
- Year 1: $2.0M (frontloaded), Year 2: $1.0M, Year 3: $600k
- Effective blended discount = 28% vs list when amortized; year 1 frontload gives more runway for adoption

I pulled together a quick list of the trade-offs we should make explicit in the amendment:

1) Early termination refund waterfall — pro rata on unused months, with an additional clawback for the upfront discount if consumption in year 1 < 40% of purchased units.
2) Co-terming — allow Acme to co-term other Redwood contracts at renewal with a one-time true-up rather than monthly amortization changes.
3) Renewal floor pricing — lock floor price for first renewal year if they renew within 90 days of term end.

I’m attaching the ACME_prepaid_ramp_v1.xlsx with the ramp math and a short redline (Amendment_redline_vMarissa.pdf) that sketches the refund language. Rafael — can you sanity-check the refund waterfall and provide the amortization schedule that legal will want to see?

Tom — if you can share who from legal should be on the thread I’ll include a clear amendment we can hand to your counsel.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ACME_prepaid_ramp_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), Amendment_redline_vMarissa.pdf (PDF redline)

Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Frontloaded multi-year prepay proposal & early-exit amendment

Marissa —

Appreciate the deck and fast turnaround. A few quick questions from procurement/finance:

- That 40% threshold for clawback — can you show a stepped reduction instead of a binary full clawback? Our CFO would prefer a sliding scale (e.g., 40–60% = 25% of discount recouped, 20–40% = 50%).
- For the true-up on co-terming: can the one-time true-up be run against the remaining amortized balance and paid over 3 months instead of immediate lump sum?
- Legal flagged the phrase “clawback” — they prefer precise refund mechanics and an escrow schedule for disputed amounts. I’ve looped legal to propose edits.

If you can send a short amendment with the stepped clawback options and a payment schedule for the true-up, we can move this to redline quickly.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Procurement — Acme Health

Date: Mon, 3 May 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Frontloaded multi-year prepay proposal & early-exit amendment

Tom / Marissa —

Thanks — I ran three alternative refund waterfalls and attached the amortization schedules. Key notes below so legal/finance have the numbers behind each outcome:

Option A — Binary clawback (baseline)
- If Y1 consumption < 40% => recoup full upfront discount on unused months; pro rata refund for unused term otherwise.
- Effective IRR on Redwood side if exercised: ~9%.

Option B — Stepped clawback (Tom’s ask)
- 60%+ usage: no clawback; 40–60%: recoup 25% of the upfront discount (applied to remaining balance); 20–40%: recoup 50%; <20%: recoup 75%
- Allows a sliding scale and reduces cliff risk for Acme; Redwood amortization schedule attached shows cashflow timing if true-up is spread over 3 months.

Option C — Usage-first with escrow holdback
- Holdback 15% of Year 1 payment into escrow, released monthly as usage thresholds are hit. If early termination, escrow is applied first to any recoupment.
- Tightest protection for Redwood but most operationally complex for Acme.

Attachments: ACME_prepaid_ramp_v1.xlsx (updated with three tabs: OptionA, OptionB, OptionC); Amendment_redline_vMarissa.pdf (annotated with suggested clause text).

Recommendation: We should default to Option B in the amendment — it addresses Acme’s CFO preference while keeping Redwood economics acceptable. I updated the redline with the stepped percentages and added a 90-day window for a single true-up payment to be split over 3 equal installments.

Marissa — if you’re aligned, I can push a clean amendment for Acme legal and include DocuSign link for signature.

Best,
Rafael
Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rinaldi <trinaldi@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Frontloaded multi-year prepay proposal & early-exit amendment

Tom / team —

I reviewed Rafael’s scenarios and ran the finance sensitivity on our side. Quick points for commercial/legal:

- Option B is acceptable to finance if we include (a) a 3-month true-up payment schedule, (b) a late payment interest at 1.5% monthly for overdue true-up balances, and (c) an audit right limited to usage adjudication within 120 days post-termination.
- For co-terming: propose language that the one-time true-up is calculated on remaining amortized balance (net of any escrow) and amortized evenly over the next 3 bill cycles, unless Acme elects to pay in full.
- For renewals: suggest a 12-month renewal floor floor protection rather than 1 year? (typo fixed: we mean 12 months) — basically lock the price floor for the first renewal year.

Marissa — I’ve attached a brief clean amendment draft (clean_amendment_for_acme.pdf) for Acme legal to review; Rafael, please confirm you want Option B inserted. If Acme legal agrees to the stepped clawback + 3-month true-up, I’ll prepare finance sign-off and DocuSign package.

Thanks,
Naomi
Head of Finance, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: clean_amendment_for_acme.pdf (clean amendment)
